assessment.summary: A present, quantified global strain — 645 million hungry and 2.1 billion food-insecure in 2025, billions water-insecure — easing slowly on the hunger side for a third year running, while food prices climb again and the escalation pathways still run through climate extremes and conflict.
assessment.timeframe: Chronic and ongoing; acute regional food crises recur annually, and climate change intensifies water stress through mid-century.

claims.text: An estimated 8.2 percent of the global population, about 673 million people, experienced hunger in 2024 (FAO, The State of Food Security and Nutrition in the World 2025).
The global prevalence of moderate or severe food insecurity was 28.0 percent in 2024, accounting for 2.3 billion people (FAO SOFI 2025).
266 million people are facing crisis levels of hunger or worse, according to the Global Report on Food Crises.
Roughly half of the world's population experiences severe water scarcity for at least part of the year (UN World Water Development Report 2024).
As of 2022, 2.2 billion people were without access to safely managed drinking water (UN World Water Development Report 2024).

The FAO Food Price Index averaged 131.1 points in July 2026, up 0.6 percent from its June level and 1.0 percent higher than its year-earlier level, with the Vegetable Oil Price Index reaching its highest level since June 2022.

An estimated 645 million people (7.8 percent of the global population) faced hunger in 2025, nearly 14 million fewer than in 2024 and 43 million fewer than at the 2022 peak; approximately 2.1 billion people experienced moderate or severe food insecurity in 2025, nearly 86 million fewer than a year earlier (FAO, The State of Food Security and Nutrition in the World 2026, launched 21 July 2026).

SOFI 2026 projects that around 520 million people could still face hunger in 2030, putting the world off track to achieve Sustainable Development Goal 2 (Zero Hunger); approximately 309 million people in Africa remain undernourished, where hunger prevalence fell from 20.3 percent in 2024 to 20.0 percent in 2025.

The FAO Food Price Index averaged 133.3 points in August 2026, up 2.5 points (1.9 percent) from its revised July level, with all commodity groups recording higher price indices than in the previous month; the index stood 3.3 points (2.5 percent) above its year-earlier level but 26.9 points (16.8 percent) below its March 2022 peak (released 4 September 2026).

description: A chronic global shortfall in access to adequate food and safe freshwater, driven by conflict, economic shocks, and climate extremes. Hunger has now eased for three consecutive years — an estimated 645 million people, 7.8 percent of the world, went hungry in 2025, and 2.1 billion faced moderate or severe food insecurity — yet roughly half the world's population still experiences severe water scarcity for part of the year and 2.2 billion lack safely managed drinking water. Food prices are climbing again, with the FAO Food Price Index at 133.3 points in August 2026 on broad-based commodity increases, and FAO projects around 520 million people could still be hungry in 2030. The tail risk is cascading food-system and water-supply failures that destabilize whole regions.
name: Global Food and Water Insecurity
